NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the critical nexus of the AI infrastructure supply chain, designing cutting-edge GPU accelerators that are entirely dependent on TSMC's leading-edge foundry capacity and HBM memory from a concentrated set of suppliers (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron). On the demand side, NVIDIA is the dominant AI compute supplier to the world's largest hyperscalers and cloud providers, making its revenue highly concentrated among a small number of mega-cap technology companies aggressively investing in AI infrastructure.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a powerful demand-side orchestrator that designs its own silicon and outsources manufacturing to a concentrated set of critical partners — most notably TSMC for chips and Samsung for displays and memory. On the downstream side, Apple distributes its products through major telecom carriers and retailers while generating substantial high-margin services revenue from platform participants like Google, making it both a hardware seller and a platform gatekeeper.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC occupies the most critical chokepoint in the global semiconductor supply chain as the world's dominant pure-play foundry, manufacturing chips designed by fabless companies on leading-edge nodes that no other foundry can replicate at scale. Its upstream dependency on a small set of highly specialized equipment makers (particularly ASML for EUV) and its downstream concentration among a few hyperscale and fabless giants make it both extraordinarily powerful and geopolitically sensitive.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology occupies a critical mid-tier position in the semiconductor supply chain as one of only three major global producers of DRAM and NAND flash memory, sitting downstream of specialized capital equipment makers and upstream of nearly every major computing, mobile, cloud, and automotive platform. Its highly capital-intensive, vertically integrated manufacturing model creates deep dependencies on a small number of equipment suppliers while serving a broad but concentrated customer base where AI-driven HBM demand from companies like NVIDIA is rapidly reshaping revenue mix.
